channel.title: The shad0w blog
channel.description: System Zero, certified LLM shortcuts, and shad0w in production.

item.title: shad0w at work: five jobs real teams can give it
item.description: Support routing, a prompt guard, product photos, a live data stream and a zero-code proxy: what shad0w does in each, the code, and what it measured.

item.title: shad0w 0.4: one reflex for text, images and guards
item.description: shad0w 0.4 takes its learned table and certificate from text to pixels, prompt-injection guards and video frames. What works, what doesn't, and what to try.

item.title: Zero-code System Zero for the OpenAI Decisions API
item.description: Point the OpenAI Decisions API client at the shad0w proxy: certified questions come back from a table in microseconds, the rest go upstream. No code change.

item.title: Snake at 120 moves a second: System 0 vs System One
item.description: shad0w, three System One decision models and a hosted LLM play the same snake games at game speed. shad0w keeps scoring; the LLM falls behind its own moves.

item.title: 94.3%, 51.3%, 0%: honest numbers against a hosted LLM
item.description: What shad0w answered, and missed, when it shadowed a hosted LLM through the official OpenAI client: wins, losses and the traffic where it should defer.

item.title: Adding a category without breaking production
item.description: A trained shortcut and a changing list of options are a dangerous mix. The rule shad0w follows, and what happens when you add, remove or rename an option.

item.title: System Zero: the reflex layer below your LLM
item.description: Below your LLM (System 2) and decision models (System 1) there is room for a reflex: System 0, a table that answers repeat decisions in microseconds.

item.title: How shad0w proves it agrees with your LLM
item.description: The certificate behind shad0w, in plain words: a held-out test, a confidence line, an allowance for bad luck, and what the promise does and does not cover.
